description:
Redwood Inference is formalizing an enterprise-grade Long-Term Support (LTS) channel for the serving runtime (kernel + scheduling) with a slower-change cadence, clear backport rules, and enterprise-friendly release notes. The goal is to reduce customer upgrade risk and operational churn for Dedicated/Private/Enterprise customers while preserving velocity on the normal release train.

Goals:
- Establish a runtime LTS branching model (e.g., runtime-1.20-lts) with defined support window, patch cadence, and compatibility guarantees.
- Define an explicit backport policy (eligibility, risk tiers, approval requirements, testing gates, and documentation expectations).
- Produce “slower-change” release notes tailored for enterprise operations (what changed, why it matters, upgrade risk, known issues, mitigations).
- Implement release engineering automation: cherry-pick tooling, PR labeling/triage, CI gating, provenance/signing for artifacts, and audit-ready evidence.
- Integrate SRE reliability gates (perf regression thresholds, canary requirements, rollback criteria) into LTS patch releases.

Scope:
- Runtime codebase changes needed to support LTS branching and backport workflow (labels, CI, release scripts, changelog tooling).
- Operational processes: patch intake, escalation path, security fix handling, and customer communication templates.
- Private deployments upgrade/rollback guidance aligned to LTS artifacts.

Out of scope (initially):
- Creating LTS branches for non-runtime repos except where required for build/release tooling.
- Major feature development; LTS is primarily for bug fixes, security fixes, and narrowly scoped perf/stability improvements.

Key stakeholders:
- Runtime org (Mateo Alvarez; Hiro Tanaka; Sofia Ivanova; Noah Patel; Omar El-Sayed; Samir Qureshi; Kira Volkov)
- Release engineering (Connor O’Brien; Sahana Iyer)
- SRE/reliability (Neha Kapoor; Sean Gallagher; Rafael Mendes; Miles Thornton)
- Product for enterprise rollouts/private deployments (Vivek Kulkarni; Lauren Bishop; Marissa Cole; Naomi Feldman)
- Support/CS inputs via escalations (Jira SUP tickets) and enterprise communications (Gmail/Fireflies).

Timeline (indicative, ~10–12 weeks):
1) Discovery & design (Weeks 1–2): branching model ADR, support window definition, backport policy draft, release notes template.
2) Tooling & CI (Weeks 3–6): PR labeling/backport automation, LTS-specific CI matrix, perf-canary gates, artifact provenance.
3) Pilot (Weeks 7–9): cut first LTS branch, run patch release candidates, validate upgrade/rollback in Private installer, iterate based on SRE+Support feedback.
4) Launch (Weeks 10–12): publish LTS docs, announce internally and to select enterprise customers, start regular patch cadence and audit evidence collection.

Deliverables:
- Published Confluence docs: LTS overview, branching model ADR, backport policy, release checklist, SLO/regression gates, Private upgrade playbook, audit evidence procedure.
- Linear project with tracked workstreams and dependencies.
- GitHub PRs implementing branch automation, CI, changelog tooling, and LTS build/release scripts.
- Slack coordination threads for decisions, triage, and release execution.
- Customer-facing artifacts via Gmail/Fireflies and linked HubSpot deal requirements where applicable.

files.description: ADR defining the runtime LTS branching model (naming, cut criteria, support duration), patch cadence, and rules for what qualifies as LTS-eligible changes.
High-level overview of the Runtime LTS channel: intended customers, guarantees, cadence, artifact locations, and how it differs from the standard release train.
Backport policy for kernel/scheduling: eligibility tiers (security, correctness, perf regression), required test evidence, reviewer matrix, and risk/rollback expectations.
CI/CD design for LTS: required checks, GPU test matrix, reproducible build requirements, signing/provenance approach, and promotion workflow.
Runtime LTS reliability gates: perf thresholds (p95/p99), error-rate budgets, canary duration requirements, and rollback triggers for patch releases.
Change-management process for enterprise LTS patches: approvals, comms timeline, customer notification templates, and incident escalation tie-ins.
Private/VPC/on-prem upgrade/rollback guidance specifically for LTS artifacts (version pinning, supported upgrade paths, and rollback validation steps).
Template for LTS patch release notes: summary, customer impact, risk level, behavior changes, perf deltas, known issues, mitigations, and upgrade instructions.
Example/pilot release notes for the first LTS cut (runtime-1.20-lts.0): included fixes, excluded changes, perf results, and known limitations.
Procedure for collecting audit evidence for LTS releases: approvals, CI attestations, artifact hashes, and traceability from issue → PR → patch.
PRD capturing enterprise requirements for LTS (support window, SLAs expectations, communication needs, version pinning), plus success metrics and rollout plan.
Living list of known issues and explicit exclusions for LTS (e.g., unsupported model families, known perf cliffs, deferred refactors).
Linear project epic: 'Runtime LTS branch & release process' with milestones, owners, and links to ADR/backport policy drafts.
Define LTS branch cut criteria and support window; align Runtime + SRE + Product; output is ADR-ready decision.
Implement GitHub labeling + automation for backports (needs-backport, backport-approved, backport-risk-high) and ensure audit trail.
Add LTS-specific CI workflow (GPU matrix + determinism checks) and document required checks for patch promotion.
Build cherry-pick/backport helper tool (CLI) to reduce conflicts and standardize commit messages and PR references.
Define and implement LTS changelog generation (grouping by category, excluding noisy internal refactors, including risk notes).
Perf regression gates for LTS: integrate perf-canary results into release checklist; define thresholds and escalation path.
Create release checklist/runbook for LTS patch release (cut RC, run gates, publish notes, tag artifacts, announce).
Private installer compatibility: ensure it can pin and pull runtime LTS artifacts; document upgrade/rollback paths.
Security patch handling in LTS: define embargo workflow, restricted comms, and how CVEs map to backport policy.
PM ticket: enterprise messaging + release notes requirements for LTS (slower change, operational clarity, deprecation policy).
PM ticket: customer rollout plan for LTS pilot (which accounts, success criteria, support readiness, and comms cadence).
PR: Create runtime-1.20-lts branch tooling and branch-protection rules; includes docs updates and CI wiring for release/* branches.
PR: Add backport PR template + labels + CODEOWNERS adjustments for LTS approval flow (runtime kernels/scheduling/release eng).
PR: Changelog generator update to produce enterprise-style LTS notes (grouped sections, risk level, links to Linear/Jira).
PR: Introduce `rw-backport` CLI (or script) to automate cherry-picks, open backport PRs, and track provenance.
PR: Add LTS perf suite baseline and gating thresholds (p95 latency and throughput) plus alerting hooks for release candidates.
PR: Publish LTS baseline benchmark set and stabilize dataset/versioning so results are comparable across patch releases.
PR: Support pulling LTS runtime artifacts (pinning + validation) and add rollback guardrails aligned to LTS version semantics.
PR: Helm values for selecting LTS runtime image tags and enabling recommended LTS monitoring/alerts by default for Private.
PR: Fix release pipeline race that occasionally publishes mismatched runtime artifacts; adds signing/attestation checks needed for LTS.
